cands.bio: Republican U.S. Representative for California's 20th District since June 2024. Served in the California State Assembly from 2016 to 2024. Earlier worked as a district representative for Rep. Bill Thomas and as district director for Rep. Kevin McCarthy. UCLA graduate with a Princeton public affairs master's.

controversies.text: Federal records show $20,000 from AIPAC's PAC since 2021; $19,804 from individuals passed through that PAC in 2025-26.
Missed 22 of 676 U.S. House votes this Congress (3.3%), counted from the roll calls through 2026-09-16. Longest run of misses: 14, 2025-03-24 to 2025-03-31.

In December 2023 the Secretary of State's office said Fong couldn't be on the 2024 congressional ballot because he had already filed for Assembly re-election. Fong sued. A Sacramento judge ruled for him that month, and a state appeals court agreed in April 2024. Fong said voters' choice was upheld. The Secretary said she disagreed.

endorsements.text: Donald Trump and the Republican Party of California endorsed Fong in 2026.
Mike Boudreaux, his 2024 special-election opponent, withdrew from the November 2024 general election and endorsed Fong.

cands.gaps: We found no documented position or action from Fong on data centers, homestead or property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land conservation, abortion, school choice or teacher pay, or H-1B visas. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in any recent cycle. We found no documented pledge on refusing donations from specific groups. Fong's state Assembly votes and sponsored bills were not available in the pages we read beyond brief mentions of bills on catalytic converter theft, controlled grazing for wildfire prevention and multilingual firearm training materials. The pages did not say how those bills fared or how he voted on other bills.

votes.bill: H.R. 1 (2025) One Big Beautiful Bill Act (final passage)
votes.what: The 2025 reconciliation law: extends the 2017 tax cuts, adds new tax breaks, cuts Medicaid and food-assistance spending, and raises defense and border spending and the debt limit.

cands.bio: Democratic candidate for California's 20th Congressional District in 2026. Former respiratory therapist for about 20 years; now a Direct Support Professional serving adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities in Kern County. Has held no elected office.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists voter-guide recommendations from Sway voting groups, including CrowdSourceCarrie Voting Guide, Human Decency, Mamdanification, The Dad Briefs' Kitchen Table, Unburdening The Ballot and Yaysayers. No organizational endorsements are listed.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Sandra Van Scotter was born or raised, or what she did before moving to Ridgecrest in 2014. We found no record of her taking a position on data centers, property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, growth and land conservation, policing, gun laws, abortion, or school choice. Her claims about managing $500,000 in budgets and advising Kern Regional Center come from her own website and we found no independent confirmation. She has held no elected office, so there are no official actions to report.

local.label: Roots 40: Her campaign site says she has lived in Ridgecrest since 2014, about 12 years; her birthplace and upbringing are not stated.

score.why: Raised $47.7k, under $50,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: About 20 years as a respiratory therapist, then a Direct Support Professional for adults with developmental disabilities. She says she has managed $500,000 in combined budgets for clients and advised Kern Regional Center. She has held no elected office.
